item.title: The climate crisis will destroy our economies – we learned this 20 years ago. When will we act? | Fiona Harvey
item.description: The radical Stern report showed that a low-carbon future is also good economics. But it seems that capitalism needs a reminder Saving the only planet we have makes good economic sense. There is, after all, no money to be made on a dead Earth. There may be costs involved now, but they are worth paying to protect our children from certain destruction. These propositions seem self-evident now. But two decades ago, mainstream economists had very different ideas. They had proved that the climate crisis would be a mere economic blip, easily absorbed by growing economies and therefore not worth… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Island Recovery After Eradication: Native forests regrow on Nu’utele; turtles and rare birds return
item.description: Nu’utele Island in Samoa is witnessing a remarkable revival as invasive rats and pigs have been eradicated. This positive shift has encouraged the resurgence of native bird species and provided safe nesting grounds for sea turtles. Furthermore, local communities are experiencing enhanced food production linked to the restoration of native plants. item.title: 3951 reproducciones · 37 reacciones | Reação do mercado - Depois da disparada do dólar e da queda forte da Bolsa na segunda-feira (26), o mercado financeiro viveu, nesta terça-feira (27), um dia mais calmo. A bolsa, que de manhã até subiu, acabou com baixa de 0,5%, depois de cair 13% na segunda-feira (26). O índice Ibovespa, agora, fica no mesmo nível de dois meses atrás. E, no mercado futuro, os juros para 2032 caíram depois da forte oscilação das últimas três semanas. Passado o período eleitoral, é esperado que os fundamentos da economia voltem a direcionar a decisão dos investidores: a entrada e saída de capital influenciando o dólar, os balanços das empresas impactando as ações e a política fiscal orientando o rumo dos juros. E parece consenso entre os analistas que o mercado financeiro têm pressa de ver ações concretas do governo reeleito na direção dos desafios econômicos do país. A economista Andrea Ângelo diz que a prioridade é cuidar da escalada da dívida pública. “O recado é celeridade. O governo precisa agir, esse novo governo reeleito, ele precisa agir com medidas concretas, sinais positivos para que o mercado mude. Não é humor que a gente está falando, mas mude a percepção mesmo de investimento, mude a percepção de política econômica que esse governo tende a fazer no próximo mandato”, afirma Andréa Angelo, economista da Warren Investimentos. O dólar inverteu o movimento de segunda-feira (26), quando subiu mais de 8%. Nesta terça-feira (27), a moeda americana caiu quase 1% e fechou a R$ 5,35. O presidente do Banco Central, Gabriel Galípolo, disse que não deve entrar no mercado para mexer na cotação: “O Banco Central sempre cumprindo sua função institucional, está ali para prestar todas as informações sobre os movimentos do mercado. Quando a gente vir, a gente vai atuar. A gente atua só em caso de disfuncionalidades, como a gente falou". item.title: Researchers discover why some frogs have escaped the current amphibian mass extinction
item.description: Amphibians are the most threatened vertebrates on Earth, with 41% of species facing extinction. In the highlands of Central and South America, a killer fungus has wiped out much of the once-abundant amphibian diversity. Yet in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, an isolated mountain range in northern Colombia, amphibians still thrive. The mountain range is home to a remarkable amphibian community of at least 48 species, including 25 found nowhere else on the planet. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Biodiversity hotspots in southwestern Germany are losing their species richness
item.description: Climate change and shifts in land use are affecting habitats and, consequently, plant diversity. To better understand the consequences of these developments, long-term and comprehensive data are essential. The "Floristic Mapping of Baden-Württemberg," coordinated by the Stuttgart State Museum of Natural History, provides a foundation for this. The data collected over five decades as part of this citizen science project document significant changes in the flora of southwestern Germany, drawing on more than 2.5 million plant observations. They also provide insights into changes in plant… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The way Earth's 'thermostat' works may have changed during Pangea era
item.description: Life arose on Earth at least 3.5 billion years ago, and our planet has remained habitable ever since—not too hot, not too cold. These life-sustaining conditions are possible in part thanks to a built-in, carbon cycle–based climate "thermostat" that controls the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. Fuente: Phys.org.
